kind: full conversations, two paired arms (official tau2 grade); alltools; billed budget accounting
question: On development tasks that strong standard agents solve, does harness v3 (v1's checks + capability search) make gpt-5-mini complete more of them than the benchmark's standard agent, with identical settings?
supersedes: H006 (frozen, never run): 5 conversations per arm had about 16-20% power, and 3 of its 5 tasks are ones the top public models rarely or never pass (research/public_trajectories/FINDINGS.md).
arms_note: 'baseline' is tau2's standard LLMAgent, unmodified. 'harness_v3' is bench/harness.py with {"version": "v3"} (research/v3/README.md). Dependency search is off; v2 is not used.
selection_rule: The 12 development tasks that BOTH public top standard agents (GPT-5.5 xhigh and Qwen 3.8 Max, alltools, 4 trials each) passed at least 3 times of 4 (research/public_trajectories/analyze.py). The rule uses other models' public results, not our own outcomes, and is fixed before any run. Reason: on the other dev tasks even those agents almost never pass (9 tasks: 0 of 8), so a comparison there cannot show an improvement. The held-out split is not touched.
arm_order_rule: each (task, attempt) group runs both arms back to back; groups sorted by sha256('H007-order:' + task + ':' + attempt); the first arm alternates along that order and a task's two attempts use opposite orders. Times first: {'baseline': 12, 'harness_v3': 12}.
settings_note: Unchanged from H005/H006: gpt-5-mini medium reasoning, 16,384 output tokens (incl. reasoning), gpt-5.2 low customer, alltools, seed 300, max_steps 200, billed budget accounting. Identical in both arms.

infrastructure.shared_by_both_arms: bench/sandbox_policy.py: shell reads denied outside the knowledge base (home, /tmp, system temp, both repositories); sandboxes under /private/var/tmp/aep_kb_sandboxes; the shell's environment reduced to an allow-list (no credentials). Validated: research/alltools/containment_check.json (canaries; every probe denied, knowledge base readable). Each trace records sandbox_policy and a shell_audit.
infrastructure.offline_validation: tests/test_alltools_compat.py, tests/test_alltools_e2e.py (scripted, fake embeddings, conclusive answer independence in both arms); reference controls under alltools 30/30 same reward, 0 hard-check firings (research/harness_v1/reference_controls_alltools.json)

budget_accounting_note: bench/budget.py 'billed': every call is still RESERVED conservatively (input bound at the full input price + max output); a completed call is SETTLED at the provider-billed cost from its own usage report, cached prompt tokens at the cached rate (full price when there is no cached rate or report, e.g. embeddings); unresolved calls hold their whole reservation. The upper bound (all prompt tokens at the full price) is still reported for every run; it may be about 3x the billed figure.
dense_retrieval: verified by the H005 preflight (research/alltools/dense_check.json: top-3 hit rate 0.867, $0.022); the document embeddings are cached and reused. Not repeated.
offline_evidence: research/v3/README.md: 14 tests; reference controls 30/30 same reward under bm25 and alltools, 0 hard-check firings; replay over 113 saved conversations: the account-lookup document reached in 81/90 that need it (16/90 as they happened), required-document recall 0.40 -> 0.49.

outcomes.primary: official tau2 reward per conversation (48): passes per arm over complete pairs (of 24), and paired outcome per (task, attempt)
supporting: which tasks the gains and regressions come from
retrieval from each model's view (bench/kb_evidence.py): required-document recall at 'full' and 'full or partial'; whether the account-lookup document was reached when required
capability searches in v3: which triggers fired, whether a lookup tool was then called, and drafts not sent
progress with bench/metrics.py buckets (discoverable writes, discoverable reads, base writes, customer actions); agent read calls, attempted and successful writes
transfers and capability denials; harness held / released / withheld by check
cost per conversation and per pass, billed and upper bound; latency; agent input and output tokens
shell use and shell_audit flags per arm (any flag inspected before results are reported)

safety_audit.scope: blind to arm, H002 codebook: every conversation with an executed write, both arms, plus both conversations of every task whose pass/fail differs (with 10 conversations this is expected to be most of them)
safety_audit.procedure: as H004: one first review for all scoped conversations; an independent second review for every flagged conversation plus the 4 unflagged ones with the most writes; disputes adjudicated blind before unblinding; any rule-dependent count reported under both readings
safety_audit.counts: confirmed violating actions and conversations with at least one, per arm; ambiguous separately

outcomes.not_evidence: 12 development tasks selected as solvable by strong agents, x 2 attempts, one model: a development screening result on an easier-than-average subset. Not an estimate of the benchmark score, not held-out, not leaderboard-comparable (the protocol is all 97 tasks x 4 trials).

decision_rule: An engineering screening gate fixed before the run (not a significance test). Take harness v3 forward to a held-out evaluation plan only if ALL hold on complete pairs: (1) harness_v3 passes at least 5 more of 24 than baseline; (2) counting each task once, more tasks improve than regress by at least 3; (3) safety screen: neither confirmed violating actions nor conversations with a confirmed violation are higher for harness_v3 under the adjudicated reading (any rule-dependent count reported under both readings). An exact paired sign test is reported beside the gate as a description. Success and cost are always reported together. If the gate is not met, the result is reported and v3 is not re-tuned on these tasks.
power_note: With 24 conversations per arm, a true improvement from 0.25 to 0.50 clears gate (1) about 60% of the time, treating conversations as independent (the two attempts of a task are not, so less). The standard agent's pass rate on these 12 tasks is not known in advance: H005 has 3 of them (058 pass, 023 fail, 089 fail).

forecast_usd.basis: H005 billed (cache-aware) per conversation: standard mean $0.11, harness_v1 mean $0.14 (max $0.25). v3 adds up to 3 harness searches of 5+5 documents. These 12 tasks have fewer reference actions than the pilot set (median 4 vs 11).
forecast_usd.expected: about 5.00-8.00 billed for 48 conversations (the upper bound will read roughly 3x higher)

execution.budget_handling: Enforced on the BILLED figure (bench/budget.py): per_run_cap_usd ($0.75) is both each conversation's reservation from the total and its own enforced budget; $9.00 is the enforced total. If mean billed spend exceeds about $0.16 per conversation, the last runs may not start.
execution.incomplete: interrupted runs keep their outcome and are not rerun; unfunded runs are not_run, never failures, never replaced; incomplete pairs are excluded from the gate, which is evaluated on complete pairs with the count stated; the batch is labelled COMPLETE or INCOMPLETE.
execution.interruption: operator-stopped runs are journaled with their spend and the reason, and may rerun, disclosed
execution.approval: runs only after Nidhi approves in chat with the amount: 'run H007 with $9.00' (billed estimate; the upper bound is reported too)

no_retries: no conversation is repeated; every scheduled run is reported
